goal: On Pi, a literal-user imm-run input (never extension-sourced input) mints the same session- and workspace-bound entry token as Claude. Enrollment and unattended batch start keep one authority dialog per entry, because a same-uid model write can forge the token; under a live token stale batch retirement and same-Host recovery open no dialog. A confirmed batch start returns the same non-blocking execution manifest as Claude, and the token is invalidated by session exit, workspace change or a pause (Spec D1-D4, D6; ADR 0025).

acceptance.assertion: After a literal imm-run input, Pi enroll and start_unattended_batch each open exactly one requestAuthorityDialog, and a declined dialog claims nothing even with a live token; a later retire_stale_batch under that token completes with no requestAuthorityDialog and records a confirmation_ref of kind entry_token bound to the plan digest; a confirmed batch start result carries a manifest listing every child's task id, Slice, risk, scope and verification commands; a rework-exit choice still opens its dialog.

Each of these is refused with no Kernel mutation: a retire_stale_batch whose only authority is input with source extension that names imm-run; a retire with no prior entry; a retire from another session; a retire after session shutdown; a retire from another workspace; a retire after the run paused.
